I have bestowed my thoughtful consideration to the record of the case.
22. The essentials of Section 304B IPC are as follows :
the death of the woman must be caused by burns or bodily injury or otherwise than under normal circumstances.
the death must occur within seven years of marriage.
woman must have been subjected to cruelty or harassment by her husband or his relatives.

sentences.text:
23. Section 304B IPC imposes a statutory obligation on a Court to presume that the accused had committed the dowry death when the prosecution proves that:
(i) the death of his wife had occurred otherwise than normal cir- cumstances within seven years of her marriage; and (ii) soon before her death she was subjected to cruelty of harass- ment by her husband or his relatives in connection with a demand for dowry.
24. I shall now embark upon the discussion as per the essential ingredients noted above.
NAVJEET BUDHIRAJ BUDHIRAJ 2025.03.10 14:49:32 +0530
The death of the woman must be caused by burns or bodily in- jury or otherwise than under normal circumstances.
24.1 The expression 'otherwise than under normal cir- cumstances would mean that the death is due to an unusual cause and under suspicious circumstances, if not caused by burns or bodily injury.
In this case, it is not the case of the prosecution that the deceased had died due to burns or bodily injury.
The cause of death of the deceased as projected by the prosecution is that the deceased died due to ingestion of acid.

This fact stands estab- lished from the postmortem report Ex.PA-3 (colly)
as per which name of the patient was Priyanka whose body was identified by her brother namely Amit Kumar and her father Ramhet and cause of death was perforation peritoritis consequent to ingestion of hy- drochloric acid.
Accused persons have also not refuted the fact of the death of the deceased by ingestion of hydrochloric acid.
The death of the deceased in such a manner would fall within the province of the death under unusual circumstances and, thus, the aforesaid first ingredient stands satisfied.
The death must occur within seven years of marriage 24.2

In so far as this ingredient is concerned,
the record of the case is crystal clear and on the part of the accused persons also, there is no expostulation.

It is an admitted position that the deceased got married to accused Ravi on 22.02.2018 as per Pg No. 10 of 19 Digitally signed by NAVJEET NAVJEET BUDHIRAJ BUDHIRAJ Date:
2025.03.10 14:49:37 +0530 Hindu rites and ceremonies and she was found dead on 18.01.2020 which is within seven years of her marriage.
Thus, this ingredient also stands proved.
Woman must have been subjected to cruelty or harassment by her husband or his relatives.
And Such cruelty or harassment should be in connection with the de- mand of dowry and soon before death.

He further deposed that his son in law Ravi did not like his daughter and used to beat her up.
As already noted in the preceding discussion, the said Ravi i.e. husband of the deceased has been declared as proclaimed offender in this case.
Thus, the deposition of PW1 qua accused Ravi is not being adverted to in this judgment.

In the cross examination on behalf of the accused persons, PW2 affirmed that her daughter never complained about both the accused persons and demand was only raised by Ravi.

She further affirmed that parents of accused Ravi used to make him understand but he did not listen to them.
24.14.

It is limpid from the afore-noted statements of PW1 and PW2 that in their deposition before the court, they have not imputed any incriminating circumstance in relation to death of the deceased Priyanka or in connection with any demand of dowry upon the accused persons.

Though, the statement of PW10 Sh. Rakesh Kumar who was then SDM, Saket, New Delhi and who recorded the statement of these witnesses as Ex.PW1/A and Ex.PW2/A shows that both these witnesses had given their statement pertaining to the involvement of the accused persons in the offences in question,
however, in view of their deposition before the court, statements made by them to PW10 cannot be accorded any significance.

25. In so far as the statement of the deceased Priyanka Ex.PW10/A to PW10 is concerned, no doubt,
the same would be in the nature of the dying declaration, but upon carefully examining and evaluating the same, it is noticed that she has levelled substantial allegations against her husband Ravi but not against the accused persons except for the fact that she referred to accused Kusma Devi as the one who abused her after she Digitally signed by Pg No. 18 of 19 NAVJEET NAVJEET BUDHIRAJ BUDHIRAJ Date:
2025.03.10 14:50:28 +0530 consumed the acid.

The said solitary statement of the deceased Priyanka cannot be read in isolation against accused Kusma Devi and in the absence of any concrete allegations in the dying declaration, accused Kusma Devi cannot be held liable for making any abusive remarks, particularly in the light of the deposition of PW1 and PW2 who are parents of the deceased.
26. The testimonies of rest of the witnesses are formal in nature which are not sufficient to place the gauntlet of guilt on the accused persons.

Thus, both the accused persons namely Ram Prakash @
Pathgaji and Smt. Kusma Devi stand acquitted of the charges framed against them.
They are set at liberty.

opennyai_summary.facts: Accused persons pleaded not guilty and claimed trial.
opennyai_summary.arguments:
Counsel for accused persons advanced the arguments that the material prosecution witnesses i.e. PW1 to PW7 have not lent any support to the case of the prosecution and in the absence of any incriminating circumstances against the accused persons, their acquittal from the charges is made out.
Ld. Additional Prosecutor for the State also submitted that crucial witnesses have not supported the case of the prosecution and the court may deliver the judgment on the basis of the material on record.

23. Section 304B IPC imposes a statutory obligation on a Court to presume that the accused had committed the dowry death when the prosecution proves that:
(i) the death of his wife had occurred otherwise than normal cir- cumstances within seven years of her marriage; and (ii) soon before her death she was subjected to cruelty of harass- ment by her husband or his relatives in connection with a demand for dowry.
24. I shall now embark upon the discussion as per the essential ingredients noted above.
NAVJEET BUDHIRAJ BUDHIRAJ 2025.03.10 14:49:32 +0530
The death of the woman must be caused by burns or bodily in- jury or otherwise than under normal circumstances.
24.1 The expression 'otherwise than under normal cir- cumstances would mean that the death is due to an unusual cause and under suspicious circumstances, if not caused by burns or bodily injury.
In this case, it is not the case of the prosecution that the deceased had died due to burns or bodily injury.
The cause of death of the deceased as projected by the prosecution is that the deceased died due to ingestion of acid.
This fact stands estab- lished from the postmortem report Ex.PA-3 (colly)
as per which name of the patient was Priyanka whose body was identified by her brother namely Amit Kumar and her father Ramhet and cause of death was perforation peritoritis consequent to ingestion of hy- drochloric acid.
Accused persons have also not refuted the fact of the death of the deceased by ingestion of hydrochloric acid.
The death of the deceased in such a manner would fall within the province of the death under unusual circumstances and, thus, the aforesaid first ingredient stands satisfied.
The death must occur within seven years of marriage 24.2
In so far as this ingredient is concerned,
the record of the case is crystal clear and on the part of the accused persons also, there is no expostulation.
It is an admitted position that the deceased got married to accused Ravi on 22.02.2018 as per Pg No. 10 of 19 Digitally signed by NAVJEET NAVJEET BUDHIRAJ BUDHIRAJ Date:
2025.03.10 14:49:37 +0530 Hindu rites and ceremonies and she was found dead on 18.01.2020 which is within seven years of her marriage.
Woman must have been subjected to cruelty or harassment by her husband or his relatives.
And Such cruelty or harassment should be in connection with the de- mand of dowry and soon before death.

5 24.3
It is limpid from the afore-noted statements of PW1 and PW2 that in their deposition before the court, they have not imputed any incriminating circumstance in relation to death of the deceased Priyanka or in connection with any demand of dowry upon the accused persons.
25. In so far as the statement of the deceased Priyanka Ex.PW10/A to PW10 is concerned, no doubt,
the same would be in the nature of the dying declaration, but upon carefully examining and evaluating the same, it is noticed that she has levelled substantial allegations against her husband Ravi but not against the accused persons except for the fact that she referred to accused Kusma Devi as the one who abused her after she Digitally signed by Pg No. 18 of 19 NAVJEET NAVJEET BUDHIRAJ BUDHIRAJ Date:
2025.03.10 14:50:28 +0530 consumed the acid.
The said solitary statement of the deceased Priyanka cannot be read in isolation against accused Kusma Devi and in the absence of any concrete allegations in the dying declaration, accused Kusma Devi cannot be held liable for making any abusive remarks, particularly in the light of the deposition of PW1 and PW2 who are parents of the deceased.
26. The testimonies of rest of the witnesses are formal in nature which are not sufficient to place the gauntlet of guilt on the accused persons.
Thus, both the accused persons namely Ram Prakash @
Pathgaji and Smt. Kusma Devi stand acquitted of the charges framed against them.
